status_summary: DOT issued a tentative decision on 2025-10-09 that would bar seven Chinese carriers from using Russian airspace on scheduled passenger and combination flights between China and the U.S., taking effect 30 days after a final order; all-cargo services were tentatively left unconditioned. Trade reporting days later said the carriers asked for more time to comment. No final order was found.

timeline.event: DOT issued a tentative decision to bar seven Chinese carriers from Russian airspace on passenger flights to and from the U.S., to take effect 30 days after a final order.

title: Deny foreign carriers a Russian overflight advantage on U.S. routes; hold China talks
uncertainties: The DOT order itself was not located; it is known from two trade reports (ch-aviation and Air Cargo News) and a wire report without a printed date. A Federal Register API term search and one web search found no final order; DOT orders under air services agreements are docketed outside the Federal Register, so a final order could exist that these checks did not surface. The Mandate covers carriers serving East and South Asia generally, while the tentative decision names only Chinese carriers. No step on withholding new negotiations with China was found.
